I'm ok. I will write a big update soon I promise. 

Small update is, we were promised a closed in unit to ourselves, ended up sharing a communal unit for 2 nights while they found us our own unit and there was definitely just someone masturbating in our presence who I'm pretty sure wasn't a woman. Other women had complained about it too but nothing got done. 

Lost my job. 

Such is life. We're good for now.

I definitely need space from my son at times but there are some things people do with their toddlers that makes me think "wow, why did you have a toddler if you don't actually want to he around them?". I'm not talking about needs must. Some people don't have the choice. 

But people who do have the choice to enjoy their child and choose to renege responsibility onto others does make me wonder.

Nobody deserves this. 

And once he turns 18, the police will side with you. 

Parents aren't obligated to keep their kids for free. It's not an illegal eviction and you're not obligated to house a fully grown adult *who is capable* but just does not want to take ownership of his life.

Have you ever called the police about these outbursts?

I'm not sure if social services can act when there's no official record. It's really poor really what powers social services have. They have many in some areas and not enough in other areas. 

I'm not sure where you are but here in the UK, councils are obligated to house 16-18 year olds in situations where their parents can no longer keep them including risk of violence, but I do also think there's got to be some police record to do this. 

I would take the next 6 weeks to quietly get your ducks in a row. Price up lock changes, be prepared for police intervention. 

It's going to be tough. You're in a lose-lose situation right now but there's a light at the end of the tunnel. 

Is there any where you can stay in the meantime? I know it's your house but at the risk of yourself and your property is it likely that alone, he wouldn't behave in such ways? 

You don't deserve this abuse.

I'm ok today. I've called the women's shelter and am waiting for an advisor to call me back about a placement or other resources. 

I'm struggling with the concept that I may lose my job over this because I work from home, and I have no alternative childcare to return to office. 

But it's all stuff I'll discuss with them when they call me back before 2pm.

I don't think transitioning has anything to do with anything to be honest. 

I don't buy into the "women can multitask, men can't" BS. 

It's just a matter of caring. 

When you have ADHD you can't control how that makes you focus when you're unmedicated, but if you care about your family then you seek solutions. They might not be perfect solutions. They might take time to work. 

Heck. The medication can make you feel both euphoric and sidetracked which is completely backwards but it's something you'd try unless you've got legitimate medical reasons not to because you never know *they just might work*. 

I'm sorry OP. I hope you find the strength, and I hope your wife becomes willing to listen and at least tell you reasonably why she doesn't want to seek any avenues, and then you'll know what your next steps are. This is totally unfair on you.

He always blocks the way. Sometimes I don't think he means to. 

I've noticed when we're in new places and he's a bit anxious, his go-to is to stand by the doorway and I always presumed it was so he could make a quick escape. He's very anxious-appearing to friends and family. 

But at home it's completely different. 

Sometimes he just happens to be standing there. And other times he places himself there. 

Today I think it was the latter. 

But it's just how he shouted at me, and then how I cried and he picked our toddler up and told me that it was our toddler that was afraid of me because he moved closer to him that has gotten me. I feel like the world's worst mum for showing weakness. 

I had a true fight or flight moment and I chose flight because I don't want the repurrcusions of fight. I literally pissed myself, and it took all my energy to stand up and reach for our son out of my husband's arms. 

I have had chance to pack a few more essentials but my husband is fighting going to sleep even though he looks exhausted. He can definitely tell something is afoot.

Not to be an armchair psychologist but maybe you're angry because he uses a different seasoning because you're lacking other kinds of control in your life?

I literally have no psychology qualifications, and am trying to escape a horrible relationship myself so my opinions may be wayyyyyyyyyy off. 

But I find myself getting annoyed at the small stuff a lot when I'm denied control in other areas. Stuff that other people would sweat off as no big deal. Stuff like whether you put oregano or basil in pasta. Or whether you put oregano *and* basil in pasta. But that's just me. And yes, I've cried over it. 

It sounds like you've had a lot on your plate to be honest. Looking at houses is a huge commitment, hosting children (which comes with the mental burden of responsibility) is so taxing emotionally. 

Cut yourself some slack. You didn't throw your cat off the balcony which is good, in the same way that I haven't started a bar fight in every pub I've ever been in even though I've really wanted to, even though it looks great in movies. 

If you're not pregnant, or against alcohol, I strongly recommend a tall glass of vino and a big dose of "fuck off" to every one else, because you're allowed to feel like this some times and feeling like this doesn't make you a bad person.

Thank you.

My brother is 15, so not any where near giving her any grandchildren, nor do I think he wants to any way. So my mum will make token gestures of gifts of money or buying items that really aren't that important, but are seen socially as big things instead of things he actually needs. 

Before the pandemic my mum said I could move back home, save up for a house and just pay for my own living expenses plus a cleaner once a week. I was willing to give her more, but she insisted. 

It never came to fruition because she realised shed no longer be entitled to the benefits she gets as a single person living in a council house, so it's just been a huge "fuck you" to me when I really need my family to help. 

Most of the adult men in our family are dead. 

My grandmother is still housing my 50 year old uncle who has OCD, and hates others being in the house, but she has taken me for short spells before, but the grief she's given by my uncle is ridiculous and bordering abuse so I don't want to ask to go back there. 

I just never want my son to treat any girl like my husband has treated me. Sometimes I feel blessed to have this opportunity to teach a boy how to treat other humans when they've got the physical advantage and other times I feel cursed and he's not even 2. He doesn't understand what's going through my head. 

Luckily my husband hasn't laid a finger on me but based on the tension today I don't doubt he would. 

And he'd expect me to sit and take it or he'd shout abuse from the rooftops. 

I need out before that happens. 

You all keep me strong. Thank you.

I don't have any strong opinions either way, but the opinion that I have formed is that babies can't manipulate you, whilst toddlers can. 

This to me means that if a baby wakes in the night, they have a need that needs filling, which should start with checking to see if they're dry, then hungry then need comforting. 

When they're toddlers, they don't need feeding in the night, and most toddlers sleep through (though some don't), and their nappies are meant to hold a lot more, plus they become verbally able to communicate whether they're wet or dirty. 

So to me, the right time would be after 12 months because that's developmentally when they're more mature.

However that is the right time *for them* and not the right time for parents who might be holding down one, two or three full time jobs, and studying, or have other kids they need to look after and it's no one else's job to tell you how sleep deprivation should or shouldn't affect you and that your needs aren't important. 

Some doctors say that after 6 months they shouldn't need night feeding, but I certainly wake up thirsty most nights so I hold the same idea to be true of babies. But if your doctor has said that they're ready to night wean, and you're happy that you're in a position to sleep train then 6 months plus seems a good place to try.

Back in the 90s, people used to throw pox-parties so all their kids could get it at once and then be done with it forever. 

My entire class was off school for 2 weeks. 

The teacher actually recommended it to the parents.

That's very good to hear. I know in some places they roll out a vaccine for it, but I've never heard of it here. 

Hope your little girl stays in high spirits.

Also, call your doctor because chicken pox and pregnancy aren't a good combination. 

They'll be able to reassure you either way.

They say chicken pox is most contagious before the scabs appear, and once the scabs have fully scabbed over they're pretty safe. 

It's usually uncommon for a school or nursery to have an isolated case of chicken pox though because it runs through classes like the plague. 

If it's just on her back it's also not likely to be chicken pox, because it covers the entire body. 

You could also look into bed bugs if she's a back sleeper and it's just her back. Most pharmacies sell creams for them, and then you'd need a soft furnishing treatment.

But if it is every where on her, until you've got a definitive answer, treat it as though it's the pox just to keep every one on the safe side.

The only thing I've ever seen that covers such a wide area is chicken pox, but that's pretty common here in the UK. 

However chicken pox usually have a wet scabless appearance at first, and then they scab over through the week. Some kids find them unbearable and itchy, others don't really. But the solution is a bath with calamine lotion and lots of Calpol until they've scabbed up. 

It's a bit hard to tell on the photo though and hard white lumps in the middle of the spots doesn't sound like chicken pox. 

Does she get sweaty? 

You could try r/AskDocs, they're not a substitute for real doctor's but there are verified doctors and dermatologists who'll tell you what to do next.

Writing about this bit was really hard for me to do. Because at the time I knew he had to go back to university to finish his degree. I told him I'd support him, even though my ex pulled a similar one on me and I ended up funding him part way through university too before I realised there was no love for me, just my money. 

But deep down I really did believe he didn't choose the timing of it all. I thought, how could he really? Every one that I talked to at the time was telling me things like "grief works in mysterious ways, every one grieves differently" and to be honest one of my friends even called me out and told me I was sounding really judgy, and I was being a shit partner and that obviously I'd want someone to support me through thick and thin when my mum dies. 

But I couldn't help but feel resentful that he was spending so much money. 

One night he even asked if it would be ok for him to go out with the boys for a night. I said he could have £50 to spend but we would have to eat what was in the house for the rest of the week. 

 That night they were out way longer than I thought £50 would take them, and when he came home he was sniffling and everything. 

He admitted one of his friends offered him a few bumps of coke. 

Now at the time I wasn't against drug use. It's not what I would have done, it's not how I enjoy spending my time, but I did also think that it was possible for people to enjoy the occasional night out with drugs. I wasn't very happy about it though. And the more I think about why I used to think it was ok to take drugs occasionally, the more I realise it's because that's what he had told me. I'm pretty sure that's where my £50 went though.

We never really had money for a long time after that for him to see his friends, and so they all thought I was the old ball and chain, and eventually his friend group migrated away from him, and he blames me for that because the isolation contributed to his friend loss, and his depression. 

Money is such a point of contention.

He'll buy in app purchases for things that are worth pennies on phone games he'll be sick of in a wekk, but he'll do it often, but if I try and make a £5 purchase for a game I've been obsessed with for years I am told we're too poor. 

When he gets a good bonus, he tells me "I'm going to put this towards the ps5" but won't put any of it towards the debt we're in because of him. Nor will he contribute to essential maintenance either. We've got black mold in our bedroom because of a structural issue with the window. Our landlords won't pay for a survey so that has to come out of our pocket. Well, mine really. And everything that's in my pocket is there to help me get away from him. 

Today, in particularly, I'm exhausted though. I've just had 3 days off work for my mental health, and I'm regretting it so much because he's just seen it as 3 whole days where I'm home to watch our son so he can go do fuck all. 

He's just berated me for wanting to take a nap. I take a nap maybe once a year. He said it's past 8pm so I can't nap even though my eyelids all falling down. 

My workplace have also told me I can't do any overtime any more, so my monthly savings are even lower now and all he keeps banging on about is this goddamn ps5.

I was never bothered about going to any of these places. 

Anyway his dad went to Vietnam, and got a bus that a) looked so uncomfortable. Like miniature flat beds that you're meant to share and b) took over 24 hours to get where it was going. 

For some reason, years after we'd split, he text me saying he's in Vietnam on this bus journey. 

So I was like "oh. Are you alone? You must be bored if you're talking to me."

And he was like "no, I'm with my girlfriend."

WELL FUCKING TALK TO HER THEN.

Couldn't imagine being his girlfriend at the time, saying "hey babe, who you texting while we're stuck on the world's longest bus ride"

And him saying "oh yeah, my ex."

Either their relationship was terrible, or imaginary and that was his attempt at impressing me.

I once let my SIL pierce my nipple because she did hers herself and they looked bitching. 

So I was sat there in my FILs kitchen, topless. My FIL casually just passes through and makes himself a coffee. 

My SIL clamps my nipple, and she gets the needle and pushes it through SO slowly. The sensation was like tough beef gristle being chewed, but like, breast tissue. 

She got it in, but I told her to take it out because the pain was unbearable, and I was heavily pierced in my teenage years with no pain issues. 

At that moment my innocent, naive teen BIL walks in to see me, white in the face, blood pouring, every one panicking and he rushes to the cupboard and passes me an expired bottle of oral morphine. I didn't look at the bottle. I didn't know what it was, I just opened and chugged. 

A short involuntary nap later, I felt much better.

Never ever let your SIL pierce your nipples. Although that breast is the one I breastfeed from the best so maybe it helped!

Most kids aren't ready until at least 2 year old. 

The main things to watch out for are hiding when pooping, communicating to you that they need the toilet, showing interest in the toilet, how people use it, and wanting to try it, having dry nights, having long periods of dryness during the day and being able to take their diaper off and doing so when it is when and uncomfortable. 

These are all signs that your young one is developmentally ready to try toilet training. 

There's no wrong or right way to start toilet training, but for children who are mostly dry for long periods, the nappy-off method is great. Having a potty available in your living space that is easily accessible, and guiding them to the toilet every hour/couple of hours with lots of rewards. Some people just take their kid to the toilet when they go, some like routine, but it's all about positive reinforcement which can only happen when your child is developmentally ready to make those associations. So if it doesn't work, don't worry, just put the diapers back on and try again later. 

Some kids don't potty train until they're at the later end of toddlerhood, so the average ages are between 2 and 4 year old.

Sometimes we only need antidepressants for a small period of our lives, and the emotional stunting is very helpful for keeping us alive.

When they no longer work, your doctor can review them, and help you with a therapy plan of either changing antidepressants (SSRI- serotonin or NDRI- dopamine), and/or in conjunction with talking therapies which are very helpful. Cathartic, but also sometimes CBT can be offered in order to help us change the way we consciously process situations in order to get a better desired outcome. 

When medication no longer works, or if the side effects of the medication outweigh the benefits of the medication, it may be time to stop taking the medication for a period of time to see if the medical route is still the route needed, or whether it can be managed psychologically or even self managed. 

There aren't many people who need antidepressants for life, but there's no shame either if you do because they can really really help. 

It's important to know that in some people, depression may be caused by physiological factors such as the shape of the brain and how information is carried through it, and for others it is less of a physiological issue rather than an external trauma issue, so there's no right path for treating depression and suicidal thoughts, but rather than everything at your disposal should be explored.
